keyQuotes: We built Un-0, an image generator powered by a simulated system of coupled oscillators.
On ImageNet 64×64 it reaches FID 6.74, matching the quality of leading conventional image generation methods when they were first published.
the oscillators are doing useful computation.
We believe it is possible to quickly push beyond Un-0; it is still early in the journey to reseat modern AI on physical dynamics and reach ~1000x energy-efficiency gains.

mainPoints.explanation: The model learns a coupling matrix and natural frequencies for each oscillator; inference evolves the system over time, and a small decoder reads out final phases as image latents.
mainPoints.point: Un-0 uses coupled Kuramoto oscillators as the core computation instead of conventional neural network layers.

mainPoints.explanation: Removing dynamics or fixing oscillator weights significantly degrades FID, confirming that the trained nonlinear dynamics are essential for generation quality.
mainPoints.point: Ablation studies demonstrate that the learned dynamics perform useful computation beyond random reservoirs or decoder-only baselines.

mainPoints.explanation: The model's performance sits alongside NCSN, DCGAN-TTUR, and BigGAN when first published, though it still trails later state-of-the-art like EDM and GDD.
mainPoints.point: Un-0 matches early conventional generative models in quality on ImageNet 64×64 (FID 6.74) and expands the Pareto frontier for small models.

mainPoints.explanation: Coupled oscillators can be implemented directly in CMOS or other analog circuits, allowing the physics of the system to compute the dynamics, bypassing inefficient digital simulation.
mainPoints.point: The work is motivated by potential 1000× energy efficiency gains through physical computing substrates.

mainPoints.explanation: The authors encourage the community to experiment with and extend models grounded in physical dynamics, noting that significant improvements are still possible.
mainPoints.point: All model weights, training code, and ablation code are open-sourced to facilitate further research.

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: Un-0 is an image generator using coupled Kuramoto oscillators as the core computation, achieving competitive FID scores on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet 64×64, with all code and weights open-sourced.
dataList.originalTitle: Introducing Un-0: Generating Images with Coupled Oscillators - Unconventional AI
dataList.summary: Un-0, developed by Unconventional AI, introduces a generative image model that replaces conventional neural network layers with a simulated system of coupled oscillators (Kuramoto model). The oscillators evolve according to learned coupling strengths and natural frequencies, and a lightweight decoder converts the final oscillator phases into pixel images. On ImageNet 64×64, Un-0 reaches an FID of 6.74, matching the quality of early leading generative methods when first published. On CIFAR-10, it achieves FID 8.76 using 19.4M parameters. Ablation studies confirm that the learned dynamics contribute non-trivially beyond random reservoirs or decoder-only baselines. While the model still trails state-of-the-art conventional generators, it expands the Pareto frontier for small models and demonstrates a viable path toward energy-efficient physical computing substrates. The authors release model weights, training, and ablation code to encourage further exploration.
dataList.title: Introducing Un-0: Generating Images with Coupled Oscillators - Unconventional AI

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: This New Yorker piece profiles a Utah repo man named Matthew Pitman, using his career and the booming RepoNut YouTube channel as a window into America’s $1.7 trillion auto-debt crisis and the brutal, unregulated world of vehicle repossession.
dataList.originalTitle: The Repo Man Coming for Your Ride
dataList.summary: The article follows Matthew Pitman, a veteran repo agent who runs the popular YouTube channel RepoNut, to explore the mechanics and human toll of the auto-repossession industry at a moment when American auto debt has reached $1.7 trillion and repossessions are at Great Recession levels. It details Pitman's methods—surveillance, GPS tagging, psychologically deft doorstep negotiations—and the physical dangers of the job (agents are shot, stabbed, killed). The piece expands into the broader economic forces behind the surge: rising car prices (average $50,000+), long loan terms (96 months), high subprime delinquencies, stagnant wages, and a fragmented legal landscape that leaves debtors vulnerable. It also examines the role of middleman forwarders, industry efforts to professionalize, and the emotional weight of losing a vehicle, which the author connects to her own experience selling her car. Through Pitman's story and interviews with other agents, the article paints a vivid picture of an industry on the front line of America's affordability crisis.
dataList.title: The Repo Man Coming for Your Ride

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: In an exclusive interview, Nobel laureate László Krasznahorkai discusses his evolving sentences, his obsession with failure, and the erosion of a sacred connection to beauty in modern technical civilization.

Krasznahorkai explains how his notoriously long, spiraling sentences emerged from a desire to mimic „explosive confession“ in spoken language, an approach he developed after years of dissatisfaction with his own work. He reveals that he considers nearly all his books failures, a perfectionism that drives him to write. The conversation explores his central theme: the loss of a transcendent, sacred relationship to beauty in a disenchanted, pleasure-driven technical age. Krasznahorkai laments that while beauty endures (Michelangelo, the Acropolis), fewer people can truly experience it. He critiques the commodification of culture and the rise of traditionalist populism. The interview offers a rare, intimate portrait of a major literary figure's mind — his influences (Dostoevsky, Bach, Japanese art), his creative process (pacing rooms, composing sentences internally), and his melancholic yet sharp diagnosis of modern cultural crisis.
dataList.title: László Krasznahorkai Writes Because He Fails

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: This article examines whether the gap between top and bottom teams has narrowed in the expanded 2026 World Cup, using data to show that while average winning margins are higher, minnows have produced resilient draws, though upsets are mostly draws rather than wins.
dataList.originalTitle: It’s the biggest World Cup but is the gap between best and worst teams smaller than ever?
dataList.summary: The article analyzes the competitive balance of the 2026 World Cup after its expansion to 48 teams. It presents data showing the tournament has the lowest average FIFA ranking (32.4) on record and a higher average winning margin (2.3 goals) than previous group stages. However, the author argues that these surface-level statistics mask compelling underdog stories, such as Cape Verde holding Spain and Uruguay to draws, and Curacao drawing with Ecuador after a heavy loss. The analysis uses historical comparisons to show that underdogs have always been competitive in World Cups, avoiding defeat roughly once every three encounters. While the expanded format creates more ranking mismatches, the rate of upset wins has not dramatically increased; most surprises are draws. The article concludes that fears of minnows being overwhelmed have proved unfounded, and the class of 2026 continues a tradition of spirited resistance.
dataList.title: It’s the biggest World Cup but is the gap between best and worst teams smaller than ever?

keyQuotes: At the same time, a few miles upstream, state law encouraged landowners to soak some of Oregon's most expensive real estate and least productive farmland, a ProPublica and Oregon Public Broadcasting analysis of water use has found.

mainPoints.explanation: Oregon's 'first in time, first in right' system protects COID's allocation, forcing downstream farmers with junior rights to lose their water.
mainPoints.point: Senior water rights legally entitle COID to divert over half the Deschutes River during drought.

mainPoints.explanation: Satellite data shows 45% of diverted water is lost in canals and 29% percolates or evaporates after delivery, leaving just 26% for crop consumption, almost entirely grass and pasture.
mainPoints.point: Only one of every four gallons COID takes is absorbed by crops; most is wasted.

mainPoints.explanation: Oregon courts rarely find waste, allowing landowners to irrigate aesthetic lawns and luxury landscapes without consequence.
mainPoints.point: The legal definition of 'beneficial use' is so broad that growing any non-native crop qualifies.

mainPoints.explanation: COID actively patrols for unused land and sends letters warning landowners to keep irrigating, or risk cancellation of their water rights.
mainPoints.point: The 'use it or lose it' rule incentivizes overconsumption to retain water rights.

mainPoints.point: Downstream farmers and ecosystems bear the cost of this inequitable system.

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: This investigation reveals how Oregon's century-old water rights law allows a wealthy irrigation district to waste vast amounts of water on grass and luxury estates while downstream farmers suffer crippling shortages during drought.
dataList.originalTitle: An Oregon Law Lets One Wealthy Region Turn the Desert Green. When Drought Hits， Farmers Pay the Price.
dataList.summary: ProPublica and Oregon Public Broadcasting analyze satellite data and state records to expose the inequities of Oregon's water allocation system. The Deschutes River is heavily diverted by the Central Oregon Irrigation District (COID), which holds senior water rights from the early 1900s. During a historic drought, only 26% of the diverted water was consumed by crops—mostly grass and pasture—while the rest leaked, evaporated, or ran off. Meanwhile, downstream farmers like Chris Casad in Jefferson County were forced to fallow fields and face financial ruin. The article traces the legal doctrine of 'beneficial use' and 'waste,' showing how loosely defined terms allow wealthy landowners—including Phil Knight's horse ranch and a luxury estate sold for $4.8 million—to maintain green lawns and low-value crops. The state has rarely canceled water rights, and COID actively monitors to ensure landowners use water at least once every five years to avoid losing rights. The report combines data visualizations, historical context, personal stories, and expert interviews to argue that the system prioritizes property rights over ecological health and economic fairness.
dataList.title: An Oregon Law Lets One Wealthy Region Turn the Desert Green. When Drought Hits， Farmers Pay the Price.

keyQuotes: Understanding each other is always more important than extracting interests.

mainPoints.explanation: The Dutch learned from the British lessons and complied with tributary rituals, receiving exceptional treatment from the Qianlong Emperor, including access to the innermost restricted areas of the Forbidden City — a privilege no European had ever received before.

mainPoints.explanation: The Macartney mission made excessive demands (such as leasing coastal colonies), yet the Qing court had already shown flexibility; after the mission's failure, British attendants like George Barrow wrote travel accounts attributing the outcome to Chinese arrogance, and this narrative became the Western mainstream.
mainPoints.point: The 'Qing arrogance and closure' narrative was an excuse the British invented for their failure, later inherited by historians like John King Fairbank.

mainPoints.explanation: Andrade points out that the Qing learned quite well during the Self-Strengthening Movement, but the government was severely aged and internally fractured; Japan, after the fall of the shogunate, gained an opportunity for a fresh start, while the massive and rigid Qing failed to rebuild itself, ultimately losing the 1894 Sino-Japanese War.
mainPoints.point: The core of modern China's decline lay in the aging of state governance capacity, not cultural conservatism or the tributary system.

mainPoints.explanation: Before the mid-18th century, China's military technology was on par with the West; Europe broke through through frantic innovation driven by intense internal warfare, while China enjoyed 80 years of peace — this divergence was the result of specific historical circumstances.
mainPoints.point: The military Great Divergence between China and the West was a recent contingency, not a long-term inevitability.

mainPoints.explanation: Using examples like Qianlong showing the Dutch mission ice games and fireworks, Andrade illustrates that diplomacy should not consist solely of negotiations — interpersonal understanding and joyful experiences matter just as much.
mainPoints.point: Contemporary international relations should emphasize 'understanding each other' and 'interesting diplomacy,' incorporating joy and cultural exchange.

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: Through an exclusive interview with American sinologist Tonio Andrade, this article uses the story of the successful 1795 Dutch mission to China to challenge the 'Qing arrogance and closure' narrative shaped by the failed Macartney mission, and reexamines the Great Divergence between China and the West from historical, political, and national power perspectives.
dataList.originalTitle: 1795 年，荷兰使团在北京获顶格礼遇，英国人为何泼脏水？
dataList.summary: The article centers on an in-depth conversation between Southern People Weekly reporter and Tonio Andrade, recounting a forgotten history: in 1795, the Dutch mission received top-level treatment in Beijing, forming a stark contrast to the failure of the British Macartney mission two years earlier. By mining Dutch archives, mission diaries, Korean records, and Qing court documents, Andrade还原了荷兰人如何吸取英国人教训、入乡随俗，最终赢得乾隆欢心并获准参观紫禁城最深处。文章进而剖析了英国随员如何塑造'中国人傲慢'的叙事，并被费正清等历史学家继承，成为解释中国衰落的主流框架。欧阳泰反驳了这种观点，认为近代中国的问题不在于朝贡体系或傲慢，而在于国家治理能力的老化与僵化，并以工业革命后欧洲内部的激烈竞争为参照，指出中西军事大分流是一个晚近的偶然事件。最后，欧阳泰呼吁在当今国际紧张局势下，外交应包含更多'快乐'与相互理解。

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: This article argues that digital purchases are revocable licenses rather than true ownership, using extensive case studies to show how content can be removed, altered, or lost, making physical media a more reliable choice for preservation, quality, and consumer rights.
dataList.originalTitle: The Case for Physical Media Ownership | Cem Dervis
dataList.summary: The article builds a comprehensive case for physical media ownership by dissecting the nature of digital transactions. It explains that most 'purchases' are actually revocable licenses, citing legal cases and consumer lawsuits. It then catalogs numerous instances where digital content was removed from users' libraries due to license expirations, service shutdowns, or platform policy changes—including examples from Disney+, HBO Max, PlayStation Store, Nintendo eShop, and Google Stadia. The piece also compares streaming quality (bitrate, compression artifacts, lossy audio) unfavorably to Blu-ray, highlights subscription price hikes, and documents cases of remote deletion (e.g., Amazon's removal of Orwell's *1984*) and post-release alterations (e.g., Disney+ edits to Star Wars). The conclusion is implicit: physical media gives the buyer actual control, resale value, and offline access that digital licenses cannot match.
dataList.title: The Case for Physical Media Ownership | Cem Dervis

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: This article traces the origin and evolution of the American Dream from James Truslow Adams's 1931 coinage, through postwar prosperity, civil rights critiques, economic stagnation, and contemporary disillusionment, arguing that its future depends on reimagining the dream collectively.
dataList.originalTitle: The Curious Career of “the American Dream”
dataList.summary: Hua Hsu's essay explores the curious career of the American Dream, a phrase coined by historian James Truslow Adams during the Great Depression in his book “The Epic of America.” Originally a vision of a society where everyone could reach their fullest potential regardless of birth, it became a national creed and global brand. Hsu examines how the dream was both realized and betrayed: postwar economic expansion made upward mobility a reality for many, but racial subjugation and growing inequality exposed its limits. He revisits the 1965 Baldwin-Buckley debate, the changing meaning of success in the 1960s, and the decline of economic mobility since the 1970s (Chetty's research shows the likelihood of outearning one's parents fell from 92% to 50%). The article also reports on contemporary indicators of disillusionment—Pew polling, Gen Z's modest hopes, the rise of crypto and prediction markets, and even the trend of Americans moving abroad or fetishizing China. Hsu visits the Milken Center for Advancing the American Dream, a museum of exceptionalism, and reflects on the gap between its polished narrative and the reality of a militarized D.C. and ongoing immigration crackdowns. Finally, he describes teaching a class on the American Dream, where students grapple with whether the dream still means anything and what alternative visions might replace it. The essay concludes by returning to Adams's original emphasis on collective self-improvement and the open reading room of the Library of Congress, suggesting that the dream's future lies in learning to dream differently.
dataList.title: The Curious Career of “the American Dream”

keyQuotes: Good architecture is not designed; it is evolved. But before you start iterating, think through separation of storage and compute, multi-tenant isolation, and fallback fault tolerance — it will save you a lot of time.

At the same time, it points out serious engineering issues like single points of failure in its monolithic Node.js architecture, lack of multi-tenancy, high resource consumption, and poor cloud-native compatibility, making it unsuitable for production-grade platforms.

mainPoints.explanation: OpenClaw was designed for a single user, and adding multi-tenancy later almost required a rewrite. FastClaw designed the (user_id, agent_id) isolation model from the first line of code and achieved native multi-tenancy through a Scope-based four-layer configuration inheritance.
mainPoints.point: Multi-tenancy is not a feature; it is an architectural decision, and the sooner it is addressed, the easier it becomes.

mainPoints.explanation: FastClaw uses a stateless Gateway compute layer combined with a storage layer consisting of SQLite/Postgres plus S3. Any pod can handle any request, supporting horizontal scaling and switching storage backends at any time.
mainPoints.point: Separation of storage and compute is the foundation of horizontal scaling and cloud-native readiness.

mainPoints.explanation: FastClaw isolates plugins via subprocesses, isolates code execution via Docker/E2B, and isolates writes via database transactions. It also implements a layer-by-layer fallback chain for LLM providers, tool providers, and sandboxes to ensure service continuity when external dependencies fail.
mainPoints.point: Isolation is the prerequisite for reliability, and all external dependencies should have fallbacks.

mainPoints.explanation: The article summarizes practices such as streamlining SOUL files, on-demand memory retrieval, periodic session summarization, and layered tool descriptions, emphasizing that an Agent that can save tokens is the only one that can survive in a production environment.
mainPoints.point: Context management is the core competency of an Agent; token awareness determines operational cost.

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: Based on over a year of hands-on experience with OpenClaw and hosting 500+ users, the author systematically summarizes the pros and cons of the OpenClaw architecture and shares core design principles and trade-offs in FastClaw's architecture, offering transferable engineering insights for Agent infrastructure design.

The article combines product thinking with engineering depth, providing direct reference value for Agent platform developers.

keyQuotes: In the two years of speculative decoding research, the focus has been on "how many drafts are written and how accurate they are," but DSpark turns its attention to another overlooked aspect: verification.

There is a vivid example of this drawback of parallel drafts: when the context simultaneously supports two continuations like 'of course' and 'no problem,' independent predictions may produce 'of problem' or 'no course'.
Under the premise of maintaining throughput, V4-Flash achieves a per-user generation speed increase of 60%–85%, and V4-Pro achieves 57%–78%.

mainPoints.explanation: By adding a lightweight serial module (Markov head) after the parallel backbone, it compensates for sequential information between tokens with extremely low latency, eliminates multimodal collision at the tail of parallel drafts, and achieves acceptance lengths that comprehensively surpass existing solutions.
mainPoints.point: DSpark balances parallel speed and autoregressive coherence through a semi-autoregressive draft model.

mainPoints.explanation: Using a confidence head and STS calibration to obtain true survival probability, the hardware-aware scheduler automatically shortens verification length under high concurrency, allocating compute power to queued requests and avoiding the waste of fixed-length verification.
mainPoints.point: DSpark introduces dynamic verification scheduling, pruning invalid verification according to load.

mainPoints.explanation: In production environments of V4-Flash and V4-Pro, DSpark significantly increases per-user generation speed while maintaining throughput; under strict latency requirements, it can leverage concurrency capacity by several orders of magnitude.
mainPoints.point: Online tests show 60%–85% generation speed improvement, reaching a new Pareto frontier in throughput and speed.

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: An in-depth interpretation of the DSpark speculative decoding framework jointly released by DeepSeek and Peking University, which replaces MTP-1 with semi-autoregressive drafts and dynamic scheduling, boosting V4's online generation speed by 60%–85%.
dataList.originalTitle: 刚刚，DeepSeek V4 新成果发布，推理速度更快了！
dataList.summary: This article systematically introduces the newly deployed speculative decoding framework DSpark for DeepSeek V4 and its accompanying training framework DeepSpec. It first reviews the pros and cons of two mainstream approaches to speculative decoding (autoregressive drafting and parallel drafting), then focuses on two core innovations of DSpark: 1) Semi-autoregressive draft: By adding a lightweight serial module (Markov head by default) after the parallel backbone, it solves the multimodal collision problem at the tail of parallel drafts with extremely low latency (0.2%–1.3%). Measured acceptance length improves by 26.7%–30.9% compared to Eagle3 and 16.3%–18.4% compared to DFlash. 2) Dynamic verification scheduling: Using a confidence head and STS calibration to obtain reliable survival probability, a hardware-aware scheduler dynamically determines verification length based on load, avoiding the waste of compute power on invalid verification under high concurrency. Production data show that, with throughput remaining flat, per-user generation speed improves by 60%–85% on V4-Flash and 57%–78% on V4-Pro. The article also points out limitations of DSpark — the fixed cost of drafting for complex requests persists — and suggests future directions. Overall, it is an in-depth interpretation with high information density, clear technical principles, and solid engineering deployment results.
dataList.title: Just Now: DeepSeek V4 New Results Released, Inference Speed Gets Faster!
